name: Number Four, Privet Drive
d: A perfectly normal suburban house where a boy slept in a cupboard under the stairs for ten years.

name: Diagon Alley
d: A cobbled shopping street reached by tapping bricks behind a pub, full of shops selling cauldrons, owls and robes.

name: The Leaky Cauldron
d: A tiny, grubby-looking pub that Muggles walk past without noticing. It is the gateway to a hidden shopping street.

name: Gringotts Wizarding Bank
d: A snowy white building run by goblins, with vaults far underground guarded by enchantments and a dragon.

name: Ollivanders
d: A narrow, shabby shop that has sold its wares since 382 BC. Thousands of thin boxes are piled to the ceiling.

name: Platform Nine and Three-Quarters
d: Reached by walking straight at a barrier between two numbered platforms. A scarlet steam engine waits there.

name: Hogwarts Express
d: A scarlet steam engine that leaves at eleven o'clock sharp on the first of September. A trolley of sweets comes round on the way.

name: The Great Hall
d: Lit by thousands of floating candles, with an enchanted ceiling that looks like the sky outside. Four long house tables run its length.

name: The Forbidden Forest
d: Dark woods on the school grounds, home to centaurs, unicorns and giant spiders. Students are not allowed to enter.

name: Gryffindor Common Room
d: A cosy round room full of squashy armchairs, reached through a portrait of a Fat Lady who wants a password.

name: Hagrid's Hut
d: A small wooden house on the edge of the forest, with a crossbow and galoshes by the door and rock cakes on the table.

name: The Dungeons
d: Cold rooms below the castle with pickled animals floating in jars, where Potions is taught.

name: Mirror of Erised room
d: An unused classroom where a tall, gold-framed mirror shows the deepest desire of whoever looks into it.

name: The Hut-on-the-Rock
d: A miserable little shack on a rock in the sea, where a family hid from letters. A giant broke the door down at midnight.

name: The Burrow
d: A crooked, many-storeyed house that seems held up by magic, with gnomes in the garden and a ghoul in the attic.

name: Knockturn Alley
d: A dingy side street devoted to the Dark Arts, with shops selling shrunken heads and poisonous candles.

name: Borgin and Burkes
d: A shop full of sinister objects, including a hand of glory and a tall black cabinet with a twin elsewhere.

name: Flourish and Blotts
d: A bookshop where a famous author signed copies of his autobiography and two fathers ended up brawling.

name: The Chamber of Secrets
d: A long, dim chamber beneath the school, lined with stone serpents and guarded by an ancient monster. Entered through a girls' bathroom sink.

name: Moaning Myrtle's Bathroom
d: An out-of-order first-floor girls' bathroom, perfect for brewing a forbidden potion in secret.

name: The Whomping Willow
d: A violent tree that attacks anything that comes near. A flying car crashed into it.

name: Hogsmeade
d: The only all-wizarding village in Britain. Third-years may visit on certain weekends with a signed permission form.

name: Honeydukes
d: A sweetshop full of Fizzing Whizzbees, Pepper Imps and Chocoballs, with a secret passage in its cellar.

name: The Three Broomsticks
d: A warm, crowded pub run by Madam Rosmerta, famous for its butterbeer.

name: The Shrieking Shack
d: Said to be the most haunted building in Britain. The screams really came from a werewolf.

name: Azkaban
d: A fortress prison on an island, guarded by Dementors who drain every happy memory from the prisoners.

name: Divination Tower
d: A stuffy, perfumed classroom reached through a trapdoor and a silver ladder. Students read tea leaves there.

name: Little Hangleton Graveyard
d: A graveyard behind a church where a Portkey cup delivered two champions. A body was rebuilt there in a cauldron.

name: The Riddle House
d: A large, decaying manor overlooking a village. Three members of a family were found dead there one morning.

name: The Quidditch World Cup stadium
d: A huge golden stadium holding a hundred thousand wizards, hidden in a wood near a campsite.

name: The Prefects' Bathroom
d: A splendid bathroom with a swimming-pool-sized tub, a hundred taps, and a mermaid in a painting. Password: 'Pine fresh'.

name: The Black Lake
d: A large lake by the castle home to a giant squid, grindylows and merpeople. Champions had an hour to search beneath it.

name: Number Twelve, Grimmauld Place
d: A gloomy townhouse hidden between numbers eleven and thirteen, with house-elf heads on the wall and a screaming portrait.

name: The Ministry of Magic
d: An underground building entered through a red telephone box. Its Atrium has a golden fountain.

name: The Department of Mysteries
d: A secretive department with a circular room of doors, a veiled archway, and shelves of glowing glass spheres.

name: St Mungo's Hospital
d: A hospital for magical maladies hidden behind a disused department store called Purge and Dowse Ltd.

name: The Room of Requirement
d: A room on the seventh floor that appears only when you walk past three times thinking of what you need.

name: The Hog's Head
d: A small, dirty, gloomy inn that smells strongly of goats. A secret society first met there.

name: Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes
d: A joke shop with a giant moving figure in the window, selling Skiving Snackboxes and Peruvian Instant Darkness Powder.

name: Spinner's End
d: A dead-end street of brick houses in a run-down mill town. Two sisters visited a teacher's house there.

name: The Gaunt Shack
d: A tiny, filthy shack in a wood with a dead snake nailed to the door.

name: The Horcrux Cave
d: A cave in a sea cliff with an underground lake full of Inferi and a basin of potion on an island.

name: The Astronomy Tower
d: The tallest tower of the castle, where a headmaster fell under the Dark Mark.

name: Malfoy Manor
d: A grand manor with white peacocks in the grounds. Prisoners were kept in its cellar.

name: Godric's Hollow
d: A village with a war memorial that transforms into a statue of a family, and a churchyard holding the Dumbledore and Potter graves.

name: Shell Cottage
d: A cottage on a cliff above the sea, where a free elf was buried.

name: The Lovegoods' House
d: A tall black cylindrical house, like a rook, with a printing press inside.

name: The Ravenclaw Common Room
d: An airy round room with a midnight-blue carpet painted with stars, entered by answering a riddle from an eagle-shaped knocker.

name: King's Cross
d: A busy London station. A boy found himself in a misty, clean version of it after dying in the forest.
